_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Castlevania (ADR-0239, PRD F14.16).
This file is data. A second game is a second file beside this one - no code
change - as long as its navigation address is read off a published RAM map
or the vendored cheat database (ADR-0184 s5: no code is invented). Read by
scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.
Rung (ADR-0239 s1's ladder). Rung 2: a published RAM selector, pinned for
the run. Rung 1 was checked first and is not available for this ROM: the game
has no stage select, no round choice and no password system, and the only
stage-select codes published for it are Game Genie letter codes ('Start on
last level', VXOLEOVE;PEEUEPLE;ZOEUSPAA in the vendored database), which are
PRG-space codes by construction and refused outright by ADR-0184 s1. Rung 3
(a save state reached by search, chain or movie) is out of this slice's scope
and is not used here.
Selector. DataCrystal's Castlevania (NES, Famicom Disk System)/RAM map names
$0028 'Stage' and $0029 'Previous Stage', and documents no value list for
either. Every value below was therefore measured against the game's own HUD
rather than read off a list: one 25 s session per value from power-on with the
pin in place ends on a frame whose status bar draws STAGE nn, and nn is the
value's title. The digits are decoded from the screenshot by tile bitmap (the
8x8 cells at x=232 and x=240, y=16) against the reference HD pack's own
'<condition>Stage0'..'<condition>Stage9' tiles, so the digit vocabulary is the
game's and not ours. 19 of 19 values matched: 0x01 -> 01, 0x02 -> 02, ...
0x12 -> 18, and the two-digit form is what the pack's own
'Stage0Plus'/'Stage10Plus' conditions describe. 0x13 and above are past the
table (the timer bytes read an impossible 1000 and the state stops advancing),
so 0x12 is the last admissible value.
0x00 and 0x01 are the 'before' side of ADR-0239 s5's measurement and are not
swept. 0x00 is the courtyard the game boots into and 0x01 the castle wall and
hall it sets once the player walks in: measured on an uncheated 90 s run of
this profile's own body, $0028 reads 00 for the first ~28 s and 01 from then
on. Both draw STAGE 01 on the status bar, which is why neither is a session:
s5's before side is stage 1, and a session is a place past it.
Against the baseline union the two differ in kind. 0x00 holds no key the
baseline does not (new == 0, s4's did-not-warp to the letter). 0x01 holds 24:
the pin refuses the courtyard -> castle transition, so the arm spends its
whole 120 s in the wall and hall while the baseline's uncheated run spends
the first ~28 s of its budget in the courtyard. Those 24 keys are left out of
the union, and they are the sweep's one deliberate omission - the value draws
STAGE 01 and s5 counts stage 1 as the before side. The pin at 0x01 is also
this profile's control, below.
The stage-clear transition is never recorded by any session of this sweep: the
selector is pinned for the whole run, so the game never observes the stage
advancing (ADR-0184's 2026-09-14 amendment). Deaths and respawns are still
recorded - the blind body dies on most stages, and on four of them it runs out
of lives and ends on the CONTINUE screen - so ADR-0184 s4 is met, and the
stage-1 route the baseline records ends in a death as it always did.
_provenanceComment: romSha1 is the No-Intro SHA1 the stage set already pins
(scripts/stages/castlevania/stage-set.json); the whole-file SHA1 of the same
library dump is 7A20C44F302FB2F1B7ADFFA6B619E3E1CAE7B546, which is the swap
byte range between the two. The ROM is the user's own dump and is never
Measured on this tree's binaries, 2026-09-26: scripts/headless_record from a
fresh `make capture-tool` and the InteropDLL dylib built from it. The
recorder's log reads the file's own iNES header as Mapper 2 sub 0, PRG ROM
128 KB, CHR ROM 0 KB, CHR RAM 8 KB, and the internal game database overrides
it with Mapper 2 sub 2 / NES-UNROM - so this is a CHR RAM game and s5.2's ROM CHR
denominator does not exist for it (it reports 'n/a (CHR RAM)'); s5.3's
reference line is the one that carries this game.
_inertnessComment: ADR-0239 s3 requires a profile's inert control to pass before a lives pin may
ride with a navigation pin. Both halves were measured on this binary,
2026-09-26, same 120 s script, same sessions that the sweep runs:
1. The lives pin does NOT pass, so this profile carries none. $002A is
'Lives' on the published map, and the map's own note - "01 = last life,
can be set to #ff but displays as 99 max" - is what the vendored database
ships as 002A:63 'Infinite lives (alt)'. The counter's start value is 4
(so the HUD draws 'PLAYER -03'), which is what the control pins.
Pinned as 002A:04 on the stage-1 value against the same run with no lives
pin: 160 of 497 files under textures/ differ - 80 backgrounds, 79 sheets
and hires.txt itself (sha256 1a378e03... against ec641a5f...) - with 3
sheet files present on one side only. The two runs' final states differ in
exactly 2 internal-RAM bytes, $002A and $074E: the HUD reads the counter
through the pin and stops drawing the digits falling. s3's sentence "It
changes only HUD digits the game draws anyway" holds for the digit and not
for the textures tree, and s3 makes the byte-identical tree the condition.
The same pair with no navigation pin at all (002A:04 alone against the
uncheated 120 s run) fails the same way, so the verdict is the lives pin's
and not the selector's: 529 files under textures/ on each side, 166 of
them differing, none present on one side only.
2. What that costs, recorded rather than argued. With no pin the blind body
runs out of lives on some stages: of the 17 swept values, 12 end the 120 s
still in gameplay ($0018 = 05) and 5 - 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0C, 0x0D and 0x0F -
end on the CONTINUE screen ($0018 = 0D), having scored on their stage
first. Each of those five's own final screenshot is the GAME OVER /
CONTINUE / END menu, and the status bar it leaves reads SCORE-003100,
SCORE-000600, SCORE-000700, SCORE-001500 and SCORE-000100 in that order,
quoted as the HUD draws them. ADR-0184 s4 wants the death and the GAME OVER
screen recorded, so this is the ADR's own trade being paid, not a defect of
the sweep; the tail of those five sessions is the continue screen and their
stages are covered by the part of the run before it.
3. There is no inert value of this selector, and that is why 0x00 and 0x01 are
the baseline and not sessions. ADR-0184's amendment's test was 'the pin at
the warp value equal to the stage the game already loads' - Contra's $0030,
which holds 00 for the whole of Contra stage 1, so a pin there is byte
identical to no pin. Castlevania's $0028 does not hold still: measured on an
uncheated 120 s run of this profile's own body it reads 00 during the
courtyard and 01 from the moment the player walks into the castle, so no
constant pin is the value the game already holds for the whole run. Pinned
at 00 against that same uncheated run: 318 files under textures/ differ,
134 of them present on one side only, and the pinned arm holds 486 of the
588 tile-data strings the uncheated run holds while adding none of its own.
So the 00 arm is the courtyard half of the same route with the game's own
00 -> 01 advance refused, and the 01 arm is the wall-and-hall half. That is
the selector working as ADR-0184's amendment documents it ('the game never
observes the stage advancing'), and it is why the two values that produce
stage-1 material are the before side of s5 rather than two sessions that
s4 would score as did-not-warp.

navigation.label: current stage
navigation.source: DataCrystal, Castlevania (NES, Famicom Disk System)/RAM map: $0028 is 'Stage' and $0029 'Previous Stage'; the map gives no value list, and $002A 'Lives' is documented as "01 = last life, can be set to #ff but displays as 99 max". Every value's place was measured on this binary against the game's own status-bar stage digits, 2026-09-26, and each value's title is the stage that measurement read. Published map, cited per ADR-0184 s5.

_titleComment: The level each stage belongs to is the published structure, not a guess: the
game is 'six levels, divided into three stages apiece, making a total of 18
stages' and each level ends on one of Dracula's minions, in the order Phantom
Bat, Medusa, the Mummy Brothers, Frankenstein (with Igor), Death, Dracula
(Castlevania FAQ/Walkthrough, video-games-museum.com, NES). The stage number
in each title is the one the game's own status bar drew during the measurement
above, which is what makes the level it sits in derivable rather than assumed.
_ramCheckComment: Each value's ramCheck reads $0018 off the session's final state. The address
is DataCrystal's 'System State': 05 = Gameplay, 0D = Continue, 01 = Title
Screen, 07 = Game Over, and the rest are documented too. It is not the
selector's address, which matters: a RAM cheat substitutes the byte on the CPU
read bus and leaves the byte in memory alone, so $0028 itself reads 00 in the
final state of every warped run however far the pin went (measured on all 19
values, 2026-09-26), and a check on it would say nothing.
What the check asserts, per value, is where the profile's own run ended: 05
for a session still playing its stage at 120 s, 0D for the five that had lost
their last life and were on the CONTINUE screen. Both are verdicts a run that
never took the select cannot produce - such a run is left on 01 (Title
Screen), 02 (Demo Mode) or 00 (Booting), and ADR-0239 s4 names exactly that
case, 'a crash screen that the new count does not catch'.
What it does not assert is which stage the run ended in, and that is measured
rather than assumed. Every one of the 2048 internal-RAM bytes was searched for
one that is (a) equal for a value in two runs of different shape - a 25 s
session whose script leaves the player at the stage's start, and a 120 s
session whose blind body wanders - and (b) distinct over the values. No byte
satisfies both: the best are stack slots at $07B1-$07C9 with 11 or 12 of 16
values distinct, and every byte the published map names collides (for example
$0035 'Rightmost Tile Section' reads 1F for stages 05, 06, 07 and 08 alike).
The reading is that this game keeps no stage byte other than $0028 itself -
the stage lives in the level data and in CHR RAM - so a check on the place is
not available here, and s4's new count is what carries the place.
A mismatch is reported beside the tiles and the new count rather than treated
as a refusal, the same way every other profile's is.
_defaultsComment: The entry is the stage set's own mint script, unchanged, run as input rather
than as a state: a navigation session starts from power-on with the pin
already set, and the boot's own stage load is what the pin steers. No save
state is used, so nothing unversioned has to travel with this profile.
The body is the stage set's own stage-1 route, repeated by
record_navigation_sweep.py until the 120 s budget is covered, exactly as
Contra's profile does (ADR-0184's amendment: effective input time, not the
cheat, is what moves the picture). It is a blind body on every stage but its
own: it holds Right, whips, crouch-whips and jumps, which is what the recorder
needs (a figure's cycle needs two turns of a hold) and not what clears a
stage. On four values it does not survive the 120 s, which s3's note above
